title: Peer Support Workers Study
official: Creating Safety in Chaos: Integrating Peer Support Workers in Emergency Departments to Support Patients Who Use Substances and Opioids
summary: Many people with high-risk opioid use visit emergency departments (EDs), facing a high risk of death if they leave before completing care. Peer support workers (Peers) - people with lived experience of substance use - may improve patient comfort, reduce early departures, and potentially lower mortality rates. This study aims to evaluate how a hospital-implemented ED Peer program can enhance patient support, reduce barriers to care, and provide harm-reduction resources in a person-centred and trauma-informed manner. The study will assess whether Peer availability and direct Peer-patient interactions are associated with improved ED care outcomes, including reduced leaving before treatment completion, as well as subsequent healthcare utilization, overdose, mortality, and other relevant patient outcomes.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Emergency Department (ED) patient at Vancouver General Hospital (VGH)
* Age 18 years or older
* Identified as using substances
* Able to receive or decline peer support services during the ED visit

Exclusion Criteria:

* Under 18 years of age
* Does not report substance use
